reviews.body:
Both added tests pass, but they only cover providers that throw on abort. The supported OpenAI Responses HTTP stream can instead close normally on abort, causing the activity to report success with a partial result.

review_comments.body:
[P2] Report cancellation when the OpenAI stream closes without throwing

When cancellation arrives after the OpenAI Responses HTTP stream has started, the OpenAI client can swallow the transport `AbortError` and end iteration normally. I reproduced this with the locked OpenAI provider and a mocked SSE response: the activity resolved with partial events and no `response_done`, because `failureOrCancellation` only runs on a throw. Temporal can then record a successful activity with a truncated result instead of a cancellation. Check the activity signal before returning the events, and cover normal iterator termination on abort in the regression test (AGENTS.md:71).

[P2] Document the cancellation outcome change for in-flight runs

With `WAIT_CANCELLATION_COMPLETED`, a workflow observes the activity's actual outcome. A model call that previously ignored activity cancellation and returned a result can now record `ActivityTaskCanceled` instead of `ActivityTaskCompleted`, changing which branch an in-flight workflow takes. The PR describes the new behavior but neither gates it nor marks it as breaking with rollout guidance for affected runs, as required by AGENTS.md:75.
